You are converting em dashes in Rust source files in /home/wink/data/prgs/rust/vc-x1. Work ONLY on these files (batch 3):

src/common.rs, src/config.rs, src/repo_utils.rs, src/options_flags/scope.rs, src/revert.rs, src/test_helpers.rs, src/url.rs, tests/cli_sync.rs, src/validate_desc.rs, src/test_tmp_root.rs, src/options_flags/por.rs, src/options_flags/push_retry.rs, src/chid.rs, src/options_flags/config.rs, src/sync/tests.rs

Task: replace EVERY em dash character (U+2014) in those files with typeable punctuation. The project's rule: the em dash usually stands in for a structural decision that was not made; make the decision. Conversion rules, in preference order:

1. Term or statement followed by its explanation/definition/elaboration: use ": " (colon + space). Example: "/// Whether the bot working copy had changes — decides whether X" becomes "/// Whether the bot working copy had changes: decides whether X". This is the most common case.
2. A mid-sentence aside set off by a PAIR of em dashes: use parentheses. "A — with everything known — B" becomes "A (with everything known) B".
3. A continuation or consequence that reads naturally with a comma: use ", ".
4. If none reads well, split into two sentences.
5. NEVER use " - " (spaced hyphen) or "--" as the replacement.

Constraints:
- A dash at the START of a line is the join for a sentence wrapped from the previous line (including inside multi-line string literals); convert it respecting the whole sentence, attaching the ":" or "," to the previous line's end if that is where it belongs.
- Inside string literals (user-visible output): convert minimally, keep the wording otherwise identical.
- Keep every line you touch <= 100 columns; if a conversion or an existing comment line in these files exceeds 100 columns, re-wrap at a clause boundary, continuing with the same comment prefix (///, //!, //).
- Change NOTHING else: no reflowing untouched lines, no wording improvements, no code changes.
- Do NOT run cargo, rustc, or any build/test command (other agents share the tree). File edits only.

When done, verify with: grep -c '—' <file> returns 0 for every file in your list (a file may already have 0).

Return: a per-file count of sites converted, and a short list of any sites (file:line) where the right conversion was genuinely uncertain, with the choice you made.

2	//!
3	//! Single source of truth for the positional `<TARGET>` forms
4	//! that `init` and `clone` accept (URL, owner/name shorthand,
5	//! path) and for the URL-derivation helpers shared between them.

13	/// A parsed positional `<TARGET>` argument to `init` or `clone`.

17	///   resolves to `git@github.com:owner/name.git`.
18	/// - `Path` — local path with explicit prefix
19	///   (`./`, `../`, `/`, `~/`, or bare `~`). Path text is preserved
20	///   literally; tilde expansion is the consumer's responsibility.
21	/// - `BareName` — a bare alphanumeric (no `/`, `:`, or path
22	///   prefix). Init resolves it via the user-config remote chain;
23	///   clone errors on it (no config-driven default).
24	#[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Clone)]
25	pub enum Target {
26	    Url(String),
27	    OwnerName(String, String),
28	    Path(PathBuf),
29	    BareName(String),
30	}

32	/// Parse a positional `<TARGET>` argument into one of the four
33	/// `Target` variants.
34	///
35	/// Detection order (path forms first, then URL, then shorthand,
36	/// then bare NAME):
37	///
38	/// - Path forms: bare `.`, `..`, or `~`; or starts with `./`,
39	///   `../`, `/`, or `~/`. `.` and `..` are POSIX cwd/parent and
40	///   are unambiguous; the consumer resolves them to a real
41	///   directory name via `canonicalize` + `file_name`.
42	/// - URL: contains `://`, or SSH-style `user@host:path` (an `@`
43	///   followed somewhere by `:`).
44	/// - `owner/name` shorthand: exactly one `/`, both sides non-empty,
45	///   no path or URL indicators.
46	/// - Bare NAME: no `/`, no `:`, no URL/path indicators. Init
47	///   resolves it via the user-config remote chain (repo created
48	///   at `cwd/<NAME>`); clone errors on it (no config).
49	///
50	/// Errors only on empty input or syntactic garbage that fits
51	/// none of the above (e.g. `owner/name/extra`).
52	pub fn parse_target(s: &str) -> Result<Target, String> {
53	    if s.is_empty() {
54	        return Err("empty target".into());
55	    }
56	
57	    if s == "."
58	        || s == ".."
59	        || s == "~"
60	        || s.starts_with("./")
61	        || s.starts_with("../")
62	        || s.starts_with('/')
63	        || s.starts_with("~/")

65	        return Ok(Target::Path(PathBuf::from(s)));
66	    }
67

70	    }
71	    if let Some(at) = s.find('@')
72	        && s[at + 1..].contains(':')
73	    {
74	        return Ok(Target::Url(s.to_string()));
75	    }
76	
77	    if s.matches('/').count() == 1
78	        && let Some((owner, name)) = s.split_once('/')
79	        && !owner.is_empty()
80	        && !name.is_empty()

82	        && !name.contains(':')
83	    {
84	        return Ok(Target::OwnerName(owner.to_string(), name.to_string()));
85	    }

1	//! CLI subprocess tests for `vc-x1 sync` — the "two machines" flow.
2	//!
3	//! Drives the whole scenario through the binary: `vc-x1 init` a
4	//! project with local bare remotes, `vc-x1 clone` it twice (trA /
5	//! trB), change + `vc-x1 push` on trA, then `vc-x1 sync` on trB and
6	//! verify trB's `main` moved to the pushed head. Raw `jj` is used
7	//! only to inspect results, never to mutate.
8	//!
9	//! The two init/clone incompatibilities this test used to work
10	//! around inline (bugs.md #1 and #2) were fixed at 0.76.0-5:
11	//! init's local bares are created with `--initial-branch=main`,
12	//! and its bot bare is `derive_bot_url` of the work bare, so
13	//! init's naming and clone's derivation agree. A relative
14	//! local-path TARGET now resolves on both sides too, so the
15	//! absolute-path requirement is gone.
16	
17	mod common;
18	
19	use std::fs;
20	use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
21	
22	use common::{CliFixture, cid, run_err, run_ok};
23	
24	/// Directory holding the binary under test, for prepending to
25	/// `PATH` so subcommands that re-invoke the binary (push
26	/// preflight) find the same build. The env-var name is
27	/// built from `CARGO_PKG_NAME` so a Cargo.toml rename needs no
28	/// edit here.
29	fn bin_dir() -> PathBuf {
30	    Path::new(env!(concat!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_", env!("CARGO_PKG_NAME"))))
31	        .parent()
32	        .expect("binary has a parent dir")
33	        .to_path_buf()
34	}
35	
36	/// `PATH` value with the test binary's dir prepended.
37	fn test_path() -> String {
38	    let orig = std::env::var("PATH").unwrap_or_default();
39	    format!("{}:{orig}", bin_dir().display())
40	}
41	
42	/// Write a minimal jj user config under the fixture's isolated HOME
43	/// so jj invocations spawned inside `vc-x1` have an identity.
44	/// Fixture state after the shared peer-push setup: two clones of
45	/// one init'ed project, with trA's pushed head recorded.
46	struct PeerPush {
47	    fx: CliFixture,
48	    tr_b: PathBuf,
49	    /// Commit id of the change trA pushed to the shared remote.
50	    pushed: String,
51	}
52	
53	/// Shared setup: `vc-x1 init` with local bare remotes, `vc-x1
54	/// clone` trB then trA, change + `vc-x1 push` on trA.
55	///
56	/// Push notes: `--no-squash-push` stops before squash-push-bot
57	/// (out of scope); PATH carries the binary under test. Preflight
58	/// is gone as of 0.77.0-3, so no stage-skipping flag is needed —
59	/// which is what removing the `sync --check` self-spawn bought.
60	fn setup_peer_push(tag: &str) -> PeerPush {
61	    let fx = CliFixture::new(tag);
62	
63	    // vc-x1 init ./tr --repo local=<base>
64	    run_ok(
65	        fx.cmd()
66	            .current_dir(&fx.base)
67	            .args(["init", "./tr"])
68	            .arg("--repo")
69	            .arg(format!("local={}", fx.base.display())),
70	    );
71	
72	    // vc-x1 clone <work-remote> trB / trA (B first, so its
73	    // main@origin is the pre-push head). A relative source
74	    // exercises the bugs.md #2 fix — both sides resolve it
75	    // against the invoking cwd.
76	    let work_remote = PathBuf::from("./remote-work.git");
77	    for name in ["trB", "trA"] {
78	        run_ok(
79	            fx.cmd()
80	                .current_dir(&fx.base)
81	                .arg("clone")
82	                .arg(&work_remote)
83	                .arg(name),
84	        );
85	    }
86	    let tr_a = fx.path("trA");
87	    let tr_b = fx.path("trB");
88	    let pre_main = cid(&fx.home, &tr_b, "main");
89	
90	    fs::write(tr_a.join("from-a.txt"), "from clone A\n").expect("write trA change");
91	    run_ok(fx.cmd().current_dir(&tr_a).env("PATH", test_path()).args([
92	        "push",
93	        "main",
94	        "--title",
95	        "feat: from clone A",
96	        "--body",
97	        "add from-a.txt",
98	        "--yes",
99	        "--no-squash-push",
100	    ]));
101	    let pushed = cid(&fx.home, &tr_a, "main");
102	    assert_ne!(pre_main, pushed, "trA's push should advance the remote");
103	
104	    PeerPush { fx, tr_b, pushed }
105	}

107	/// Assert trB ended in the fully-synced state: work-repo `main` at
108	/// the pushed head with `@` repositioned onto it, and the bot
109	/// repo's `@` repositioned onto its `main`.
110	fn assert_trb_synced(p: &PeerPush) {
111	    let home = &p.fx.home;
112	    assert_eq!(
113	        cid(home, &p.tr_b, "main"),
114	        p.pushed,
115	        "trB's main should move to trA's pushed head"
116	    );
117	    assert_eq!(
118	        cid(home, &p.tr_b, "@-"),
119	        p.pushed,
120	        "trB's @ should be repositioned onto the new main"
121	    );
122	    let bot = p.tr_b.join(".claude");
123	    assert_eq!(
124	        cid(home, &bot, "@-"),
125	        cid(home, &bot, "main"),
126	        "trB/.claude's @ should be repositioned onto its main"
127	    );
128	}

131	/// must end fully synced — main at trA's pushed head, `@`
132	/// repositioned in both repos. Encodes the t1A/t1B transcript
133	/// (2026-07-02) where the pre-0.67.0 check-mode default left `@-`
134	/// on the pre-fetch tip; red until 0.67.0-2 made sync single-mode.
135	#[test]
136	fn cli_sync_default_moves_main_and_at_after_peer_push() {
137	    let p = setup_peer_push("sync-default-peer-push");
138	    run_ok(
139	        p.fx.cmd()
140	            .current_dir(&p.tr_b)
141	            .env("PATH", test_path())
142	            .arg("sync"),

145	}
